tier_reason: Benchmark code is public (benches/throughput.rs calling the simdutf crate via FFI, driven by scripts/bench_hosts.sh), the toolchain is rustc nightly (rust-toolchain.toml) with release profile lto="thin" and RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native", and the Apple M4 Max host is a named CPU model. Tier A rests on the M4 Max rows; the 'Xeon x86-64' rows lack a CPU model.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Author: 'beats simdutf across nearly the entire grid, ASCII included, roughly 1.5-2x ahead on typical text, and 3-10x ahead on emoji-heavy input.' README tables (vs simdutf's validating entry points): UTF-32->UTF-8 emoji-4b 18.0 vs 4.6 GB/s (+294.0%) on Apple M4 Max and 30.5 vs 3.2 GB/s (+853.9%) on Xeon; UTF-8->UTF-16 cjk-3b 8.1 vs 6.7 GB/s (+20.1%) on Xeon and 9.7 vs 8.0 GB/s (+20.9%) on M4 Max. Across non-emoji transcoding rows the margin over simdutf ranges from -1.1% to +57.9%, below the headline 1.5-2x; the 3-10x emoji gains appear only for UTF-16/UTF-32 -> UTF-8 (UTF-8 -> UTF-16/32 emoji rows are +2.8% to +61.3%).
corrections.workload: UTF-8/UTF-16/UTF-32 transcoding against simdutf (Rust `simdutf` 0.7.0 crate, C++ via FFI, validating convert_* entry points), encoding_rs and std char iterators, plus grapheme iteration, width/truncation, word wrap and equality against Rust crates (unicode-segmentation, unicode-width, textwrap, memcmp) on ~1 MiB ascii/cjk/emoji corpora; custom best-of-7 ratio harness in benches/common.rs (optional divan mode), not criterion; Apple M4 Max and a 'Xeon x86-64' host
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc nightly (rust-toolchain.toml channel = "nightly", exact version not pinned) via `cargo bench`, release profile lto = "thin", RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native" (scripts/bench_hosts.sh)
corrections.caveats: Second benchmark host is labeled only 'Xeon x86-64' (no CPU model), and the nightly toolchain version is not pinned. The headline '1.5-2x on typical text' exceeds the README tables, where non-emoji transcoding margins over simdutf are -1.1% to +57.9%; the 3-10x emoji wins apply only to UTF-16/UTF-32 -> UTF-8. simdutf's validation-skipping convert_valid_* results are measured (recorded as 'simdutf-valid' in benches/data/*.jsonl) but excluded from the README tables. Grapheme/width/wrap/equality comparisons are against Rust crates, not simdutf. Very young project with 10 stars; requires nightly Rust.

notes: Numbers verified in README raw tables; one percentage in the record was misattributed (Xeon UTF-8->UTF-16 cjk-3b is +20.1%, +20.9% is the M4 Max row). Record said criterion; the harness is custom (divan optional). Metadata (MIT, 10 stars, last commit 2026-09-03, not fork/archived) confirmed.

tier_reason: First-party Google Benchmark results (sources in perf/transcoding_perf.cpp, perf/normalize_perf.cpp, perf/icu_normalization.cpp) with only 'GCC on Linux' stated: no CPU model, compiler version or flags, so C. Values exist only as SVG bar charts, but bar widths on the 0-2,500,000 ns axis make them derivable.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Author text: '[Text] is factors faster than ICU's UTF-8 code path, and a bit faster than ICU's much faster UTF-16 code path' (NFC normalization of NFC-input European text); 'In every case, [Text] is faster than the UTF-8 ICU code path.' Chart bar widths (derived from page data): NFC European from NFC ~474k ns (Text string append) vs ~588k ns ICU UTF-8 (~1.24x) vs ~476k ns ICU UTF-16 (parity); in the other three NFC scenarios Text beats ICU UTF-8 by only ~1.02-1.13x and ICU UTF-16 is faster (e.g. non-European from NFD ~893k vs ~558k ns). UTF-8->UTF-16 transcoding: Text SIMD ~473k ns vs ICU ~476k ns (parity); Text no-SIMD ~590k ns (slower than ICU).
corrections.workload: UTF-8->UTF-16 and UTF-8->UTF-32 transcoding (ICU compared only for UTF-8->UTF-16 via UnicodeString::fromUTF8) and NFC/FCC/NFD normalization of ~0.5 MB Wikipedia text (European and non-European, NFC-input and NFD-input) against ICU's UTF-8 and UTF-16 normalizers; Google Benchmark
corrections.caveats: Only 'GCC on Linux' stated: no CPU model, compiler version or flags; results appear only as SVG bar charts (doc copyright 2020, run date not given). The 'factors faster' text overstates the charts: best case is ~1.24x vs ICU's UTF-8 normalizer and parity with ICU's UTF-16 normalizer, and ICU UTF-16 wins the other three NFC scenarios. The latest commit (dd2959e, 2024-01-18, issue #212) force-disables the SIMD transcoding path, so current code runs the 'no SIMD' path that the chart shows slower than ICU for UTF-8->UTF-16. No commits since Jan 2024.

notes: Quoted sentences are on performance.qbk, but the SVG bar geometry shows modest gains (1.02-1.24x vs ICU UTF-8 normalization) and losses to ICU UTF-16 in 3 of 4 NFC cases; downgraded for overstated claim, tier stays C. The record's caveat that results are 'worse than ICU' for non-European/NFD input holds only against ICU's UTF-16 path, not its UTF-8 path. Metadata (BSL-1.0, 346 stars, last commit 2024-01-18) confirmed.

tier_reason: README has a first-party per-file ms table against ICU4C 65.1 via text-icu, and benchmark code is public (benchmark/Benchmark.hs, benchmark/NormalizeFile.hs). Only 'macOS' is stated, with no CPU model, GHC version or flags, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Up to +376.87% (NFKD/Korean: 7.78 ms vs ICU 37.10 ms, ~4.8x). Wins all 14 NFD/NFKD rows (+8.82% to +376.87%) but only 5 of 14 NFC/NFKC rows; ICU is faster in 9 of 28 rows, e.g. NFC/Japanese -292.04% (11.90 vs 3.04 ms), NFC/AllChars -171.63%, NFC/Deutsch -54.39%, NFC/English -7.21%.
corrections.caveats: No CPU model, GHC version, or compiler flags are stated (only 'macOS'), so capped at Tier C. Results are mixed: unicode-transforms wins every decomposition (NFD/NFKD) row, but ICU is faster in 9 of 14 composition (NFC/NFKC) rows, including NFC for English, Deutsch, Korean, Japanese and AllChars. ICU is called through the text-icu Haskell binding. The table is for v0.3.7 (current package version is 0.4.0.1), with no run date.
